lead.headline: At least 17 people are killed in a crush at a Durga Puja gathering in Kolkata as sudden rain sends crowds running for shelter
lead.short: At least 17 people were killed and 25 injured in a crush at a Durga Puja event in Kolkata, officials said, after sudden rainfall sent a surge of people looking for shelter. Later reports put the toll at 19. West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendhu Adhikari said a seven-year-old girl was among the dead.

why.text: It is the second deadly crowd disaster at a festival in a day, after a truck ploughed into devotees in Gwalior.

more: A senior police official told AFP that an announcement caused "commotion" once it started raining, and the crowd began "pushing, pulling and rushing forward and fell on the ground, leading to the stampede". Prime Minister Narendra Modi called it a "tragic" incident and said the state government was helping the families.

Early on Sunday in Gwalior, Madhya Pradesh, a truck crashed into devotees waiting near a temple, killing 14 and injuring nearly 40, according to the Prime Minister's office. Modi announced ₹2 lakh for the family of each person killed and ₹50,000 for each of the injured.
Two years ago, 121 people died in a crush at a religious gathering in Uttar Pradesh.

seconds.headline: At least seven are reported killed and dozens hurt as a live-fire drill sets off a blaze at a Canadian army base
seconds.short: A fire at Canadian Forces Base Wainwright in Alberta, one of the country's busiest training bases, killed and injured several people on Saturday, Defence Minister David McGuinty said. Global News, citing military sources, reported at least seven dead and dozens injured after a live-fire exercise hit a gas line or gas well.

why.text: McGuinty said he could not recall an incident like it, and Edmonton's main hospital declared a disaster code.

more: High winds spread the fire rapidly and it tore through the base's fences, the Municipal District of Wainwright said. McGuinty called the situation "very, very active and delicate" and gave no cause or casualty figure. Prime Minister Mark Carney said a "serious incident creating a major fire" had occurred.

Royal Alexandra Hospital in Edmonton called a code orange, its protocol for mass casualties. "It is more patients than any of us want to count right now. It's a disaster," emergency doctor Warren Thirsk told the CBC.
Saskatchewan's premier Scott Moe said he had sent resources and was ready to send more.

facts.cause: unconfirmed; drill reportedly hit a gas line

seconds.headline: More than 1,200 are arrested as protests over schools and living costs turn violent across France and Limoges town hall burns
seconds.short: At least 1,200 people were arrested on Saturday as an estimated 550,000 marched across France against hardship in schools and the cost of living. Buildings were set alight in Paris and other cities, looting broke out, and a fire at Limoges town hall caused its roof to partly collapse. Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu said 150 police were injured.

why.text: Weeks of school students' protests have grown into nationwide unrest that the government calls an escalation in violence.

more: In Paris the main march was largely peaceful in the afternoon, but by evening groups were torching cars at Place de la République and riot police used tear gas and water cannon. In Lyon, the tourist office burned. "It breaks our hearts," mayor Grégory Doucet said.

In Saint-Étienne a young man "had his hand blown off" by a small explosive, mayor Régis Juanico said. Students have protested for weeks over staff shortages and run-down lycées, the secondary schools for 15 to 18-year-olds, and trade union members have swelled their numbers. Local police in Lyon said "hostile individuals" kept firefighters away from the blaze.
Donald Trump mocked the unrest on social media, NDTV reported.

seconds.headline: Rubio lands in India but skips Delhi, meeting Jaishankar in Mumbai, as Trump says 'a lot of you don't know' what his sanctions decision means
seconds.short: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio arrives in India on Sunday and will hold talks with S. Jaishankar in Mumbai on Monday, then visit Reliance's Jamnagar refinery, without stopping in Delhi. Opposition leaders say Jaishankar is being "summoned" on home soil after the US ambassador said Washington expected him to travel to Rubio.

why.text: The visit is the first high-level contact since Trump waived the 100% tariff threat over India's Russian oil.

more: The foreign ministry's Randhir Jaiswal said the Mumbai talks would cover energy, trade and investment, defence and emerging technologies. In Jamnagar, Rubio is due to attend a reception hosted by the Ambani family, The Hindu reported. He comes from a summit with five Central Asian states in Samarkand.

At Mar-a-Lago on Saturday, Trump defended the order he signed on Friday. "A lot of you don't know what my decision is yet, but we'll figure it out," he said. Rubio said the President wanted 60 days to study the sanctions law's impact. The order's waivers last until the President or Secretary of State decides otherwise.

update.new: Rubio arrives for talks in Mumbai and Jamnagar; Trump defends the waiver and wants 60 days to study the law.
update.front: Washington's top diplomat is in India two days after the tariff threat was shelved, and where he chose to meet has become a row.

seconds.headline: Settlers attack European diplomats' cars and a French mayor in the West Bank, a day after beating a Washington Post photographer
seconds.short: Israeli settlers attacked vehicles carrying French, Belgian and Polish diplomats near Taybeh in the occupied West Bank on Saturday, and beat a visiting 78-year-old French mayor who was helping Palestinians harvest olives. On Friday, masked settlers kicked Washington Post photographer Heidi Levine, an American, for what she said was at least 10 minutes.

why.text: Washington and European governments are now protesting attacks on their own citizens and envoys, not only on Palestinians.

more: Bernard Baudoux, mayor of Aulnoye-Aymeries, said he was kicked and hit with iron bars. "I was thrown to the ground," he told Reuters. Belgian Foreign Minister Maxime Prevot said: "Impunity for violent settlers must end." Benjamin Netanyahu said there was no "compelling evidence" about the attack on the diplomats.

Levine had surgery at Beilinson Hospital and said her camera and phone were stolen. Marco Rubio said Donald Trump was "very disturbed by those images", and US ambassador Mike Huckabee said the attackers "should spend YRS in prison". Israel's foreign minister Gideon Saar condemned the attack on the diplomats but said they should have coordinated their visit with the army.

update.new: Settlers attacked European diplomats and a French mayor, and a US photojournalist needed surgery.
update.front: The attacks have reached foreign diplomats and an American journalist, drawing protests from Washington and Brussels.

briefs.text: "Abhijeet Dipke released," the party's legal chief Ratna Singh posted on Saturday. Two other CJP leaders are due out on Sunday. Dipke, 31, said on Instagram he "knew going to jail was inevitable".

stories.headline: Pope Leo leaves hospital four days after lung cancer surgery and walks unaided to his car
stories.short: Pope Leo XIV, 71, was discharged from Rome's Gemelli Hospital on Saturday, four days after a 90-minute operation that removed the lower lobe of his right lung. He walked unaided to his car and stopped to talk to well-wishers. The Vatican said he would lead the Angelus prayer in St Peter's Square on Sunday.

why.text: His schedule had been cleared until 20 October, so his return is earlier than the Vatican had planned for.

more: His doctors said blood tests and a chest X-ray showed "steady improvement". Results of tests to check whether the cancer has spread have not been announced. Those close to him say he does not want to delay a trip to Latin America in early November, including Peru, where he was a missionary.

On Friday he spoke to Vladimir Putin, their first call since June 2025, to urge "dialogue and peace", the Vatican said. He also called for a humanitarian ceasefire in Oleshky, a Russian-occupied Ukrainian town under constant shelling, so people could be evacuated and food and medicine delivered. The BBC has reported residents there eating garden weeds to survive.

update.new: The Pope left hospital four days after surgery and spoke to Putin.

stories.headline: Jio Platforms sets a price band of ₹1,065 to ₹1,119 for an IPO worth up to ₹30,213 crore, which would be India's biggest
stories.short: Reliance's telecom and digital arm will sell shares at ₹1,065 to ₹1,119 each, raising up to ₹30,213 crore at the top of the band, which could make it India's biggest IPO. Anchor investors bid on Monday 19 October, and the issue is open to the public from 21 to 23 October.

why.text: An issue this size will draw money from across the market in the week it opens.

more: The offer is a fresh issue of up to 27 crore shares. Unofficial grey-market trading puts a premium of ₹235 on each share, pointing to a listing around 21% above the issue price, Mint reports. That premium has swung by ₹87 over the past 15 sessions without a clear trend.

Its subsidiary Reliance Jio Infocomm had 533.3 million customers at 30 June, and 284.9 million 5G subscribers in the April to June quarter, the world's third-largest 5G base. Jio was the first Indian operator to roll out a standalone 5G network. The company, set up in November 2019, also runs broadband, cloud, enterprise and AI services.

update.new: Jio set its price band and dates: anchors bid on 19 Oct, the public from 21 to 23 Oct.

briefs.headline: HDFC Bank's profit rises 5% to ₹19,510 crore, and deputy MD Kaizad Bharucha will step down on 31 December
briefs.text: Net interest income grew 10% in July to September. Bharucha, a candidate for chief executive, would have hit the RBI's 15-year cap in 2029; Anup Bagchi from ICICI takes over as CEO on 27 October.

briefs.headline: Tesla opens Roadster reservations in India at ₹50 lakh, or ₹2.5 crore for the version with thrusters
briefs.text: Buyers pay a refundable ₹5.01 lakh, then the rest within 10 days. Production starts in 2028 with left-hand drive only, and Tesla has not given an India delivery date. Thrusters may not be allowed in every market.

briefs.headline: Anthropic is asking law firms how lawyers negotiate, to write rules for AI agents that bargain for their users
briefs.text: Agents could one day haggle over prices, customer complaints or salary offers, the Financial Times reported, citing two people. Anthropic is studying "negotiating norms" for when agents represent users whose interests clash.

stories.headline: Japan is set to launch the first mission to bring back soil from Phobos, one of the two small moons of Mars
stories.short: Japan's space agency, JAXA, aims to launch its Martian Moons eXploration spacecraft on an H3 rocket on Tuesday, on a five-year mission to collect samples from Phobos and bring them back to Earth. NASA and other agencies are supplying equipment and communications support. Several Russian attempts to land on Phobos have failed.

why.text: Scientists hope the samples will settle whether the Martian moons are debris from an impact on Mars or captured asteroids.

more: "They are known as the most important unclimbed mountains in the solar system," said project manager Yasuhiro Kawakatsu. He said the samples would also help scientists judge whether a Martian moon could serve as a base for crewed missions to the planet.

"We can almost certainly come to a conclusion by analysing soil samples," said Kiyoshi Kuramoto, the mission's principal investigator. Phobos was chosen over Deimos because it is closer to Mars, and about 0.1% of the material collected is expected to come from Mars itself. Phobos is about 27km across at its widest. Since the 1960s dozens of missions have gone to Mars, but its moons remain largely unexplored.

briefs.headline: Apple Stores are told to warn shoppers there will be no iPhone Duo stock for walk-ins on launch day
briefs.text: Staff told MacRumors they should discourage customers without pre-orders from coming in on Friday 23 October. Nikkei Asia reported in September that production had reached only a few hundred phones a day.

stories.headline: Maresca becomes the first Premier League manager to win his first seven games as City beat Ipswich 3–2 and go six clear
stories.short: Manchester City beat Ipswich 3–2 on Saturday as Enzo Maresca became the first manager in Premier League history to win his first seven games. Erling Haaland scored twice, and City moved six points clear at the top. It was their first home league game since the club was found to have broken financial rules.

why.text: City are top and winning despite the guilty verdict hanging over the club.

more: Phil Foden, a local boy, started the win and kissed the badge, and Haaland secured it after Ipswich twice threatened through Daizen Maeda and Zian Flemming. "I didn't expect to win seven out of seven, but we are working well," Maresca said. "This is the most important thing." Most of the home crowd has responded to the verdict with defiance.

The win came at a cost. Haaland and Antoine Semenyo limped off at full time, and Mateo Kovacic, Matheus Nunes and Nico O'Reilly were also injured. Maresca was unsure how serious the injuries were, with AEK Athens visiting on Tuesday in the Champions League.

briefs.headline: Chelsea's Emi Martínez has surgery after a collision with Everton's Branthwaite, as Neto's double ends Everton's unbeaten start
briefs.text: The goalkeeper said after Saturday's 2–0 win that he expects to be back in a few weeks. He was hurt when he and Jarrad Branthwaite came together under a Dewsbury-Hall free kick.

briefs.headline: Mourinho says he would have left Spain long ago if he were Vinícius, as Madrid host Sevilla without him tonight
briefs.text: "Tremendous credit to him for the fact that he keeps living and surviving and still having a smile," Mourinho said. Vinícius starts a four-match ban that covers the Clásico; Madrid have 18 points from eight games.

briefs.headline: Daniel Dubois stops Fabio Wardley in two rounds at the O2 to keep his WBO heavyweight title
briefs.text: IBF champion Filip Hrgovic climbed into the ring afterwards wanting a rematch. Promoter Frank Warren said Dubois would chase a unification fight next year, possibly with the winner of Fury and Joshua in December.

briefs.headline: Bayern beat RB Leipzig 6–1 with a Luis Díaz hat-trick, days before Leipzig face Real Madrid
briefs.text: Bayern outshot Leipzig 29 to 12 and led 14 shots to none at half-time. Díaz added an assist and Harry Kane made two. Leipzig, under new coach Martín Demichelis, lost 4–1 at Como in the Champions League.

briefs.headline: Into the Wuhan Open final: Kartal saves six set points against Ostapenko and plays Maja Chwalinska for the title today
briefs.text: She saved six set points to win 7-6 (11-9) 7-6 (7-5), becoming the lowest-ranked WTA 1000 finalist. Chwalinska beat Iga Swiatek. The final starts at 4pm IST today, and Kartal will be British number one on Monday.

briefs.text: The fifth T20I, Bengaluru's first international in two years, was abandoned midway after fans braved rain and traffic. India's next match is the first T20I against New Zealand in Christchurch on Thursday.

update.new: The decider was abandoned; the series finished 2–2.
